questions.question: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?
questions.rationale: This is the primary objective. Civil birth registrations (actas de nacimiento) in Michoacán were recorded at the municipal level from 1859 onward and routinely name both parents; Catholic baptismal registers for Nueva Italia (a Purépecha-region colonization settlement) and nearby parishes in the Tepalcatepec/Apatzingán corridor similarly name both parents and godparents. These are the highest-yield direct sources. Nueva Italia was established as an agricultural colony around 1900–1903 by the Cusi family and populated largely from Jalisco and other Michoacán localities, so records may also exist in origin parishes. The siblings already in the tree (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) may appear in the same household and corroborate the family unit.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two original civil birth registrations from Guerrero (CID 1918291) directly name Sóstenes Cruz as father and Apolinar Corona as mother: (1) Mauro Cruz Corona, born 22 Nov 1910, La Unión, Guerrero, registered 6 Dec 1910, father Sóstenes Cruz declarant (src_001, ark:/61903/1:1:QGWQ-MCFV); (2) Margarito Cruz Corona (sibling), born 10 Jun 1908, La Unión, Guerrero, registered 17 Jun 1908, same parents (src_002, ark:/61903/1:1:QGW7-YQNS). The subject's own birth record — the decisive record type for a parentage question — was found in the correct jurisdiction (Guerrero civil registration, which began in 1860 per the Mexico Civil Registration wiki). Michoacán civil registration (CID 1916243) was also searched and returned no record, explained by the actual Guerrero birthplace. The 1930 Mexico census was searched with a negative result. Three planned fallback/ancillary items (pli_004 Michoacán Catholic church records, pli_005 Ancestry alternate Michoacán index, pli_007 US border crossings) were not searched, but all are either fallbacks for a now-successful primary search or ancillary records incapable of naming different parents — none constitutes an unsearched gap that could overturn the conclusion. The breadth of search spans two states, two repositories, and two record types (civil registration + census). All seven stop criteria are met.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. Two original Guerrero civil birth registrations (Mauro 1910, sibling Margarito 1908) directly and explicitly name both parents: father Sóstenes Cruz, mother Apolinar Corona. The question is answered with a convincing, corroborated response from the highest-quality source type available.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. The actual jurisdiction of the birth event (La Unión, Guerrero) was searched in CID 1918291 — positive result. The initially assumed jurisdiction (Michoacán, CID 1916243, three searches with name variants) was also searched — negative, consistent with the actual Guerrero location. The 1930 Mexico census (CID 1307314) was searched — negative. Three unsearched plan items (pli_004, pli_005, pli_007) are fallback or ancillary searches: pli_004 and pli_005 are explicitly marked fallback_for pli_001, which succeeded; pli_007 (US border crossings) is ancillary and could not name different parents. No primary repository for the confirmed event jurisdiction remains unsearched.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. Both sources are original civil registration documents (actas de nacimiento) from CID 1918291, accessed as images on FamilySearch. No derivative or transcription has been substituted for an original.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Two sources cover this question: Mauro's own 1910 birth registration (src_001) and sibling Margarito's 1908 birth registration (src_002). These are separate registration acts, conducted on different dates (6 Dec 1910 vs. 17 Jun 1908), for different individuals, each independently entered in the Guerrero civil register by the official civil registrar. Even on the conservative assumption that the private informant was the same person (the father) in both, the civil registrar's independent institutional recording of each event constitutes at least one independent evidentiary unit beyond the family informant.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. Both records are original civil registrations (created contemporaneously, within days of the births) with primary information (reported by persons with firsthand knowledge of the event). The subject's own birth record (src_001) is original and primary — the strongest possible source class for a parentage question.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No formal conflicting records exist (0 conflicts registered). The discrepancy between the question's premise ('Nueva Italia, Michoacán') and the records' stated birthplace ('La Unión, Guerrero') is a conflict between a secondary/oral premise and two original records — both records agree, no competing document names different parents or a different birthplace. The discrepancy is documented in h_001 and flagged for proof-conclusion to address; it does not constitute an unresolved conflict between independent sources. The uncertain reading of the mother's surname in Mauro's 1910 record ('Co??na') is resolved by the 1908 sibling record, which spells 'Corona' clearly.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The subject's own original civil birth registration has been found in the correct jurisdiction. Both found records agree on both parents. No competing record naming different parents exists anywhere in the corpus. The three unsearched plan items (pli_004 Michoacán Catholic fallback, pli_005 Ancestry alternate Michoacán index, pli_007 US border crossings) either search the wrong jurisdiction for this event or are ancillary sources that could corroborate but not overturn the established parentage. Guerrero Catholic baptismal records for 1910 could theoretically exist, but given the civil registration's coverage from 1860 and the positive finding, a baptism record would be corroborative, not overturning. No known, accessible, unsearched record type for the confirmed event jurisdiction could plausibly name different parents.

## Proof Argument: Parentage of Mauro Cruz Corona (born 22 November 1910)

### Research Question

Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?

### Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence strongly suggests that Mauro Cruz Corona was the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (father) and **Apolinar Corona** (mother). This conclusion rests on five records spanning two original civil birth registrations and three Catholic marriage register index entries, all of which name the same parents with consistent detail across two states (Guerrero and Michoacán) and across three decades (1908–1945). The tier is **probable** rather than proved because the three Catholic marriage records are derivative (index-only; underlying images not examined), and the identity correlation between the Guerrero-born child of the civil register and the adult Mauro Cruz who married in Michoacán in 1941, while now strongly supported, rests in part on secondary-quality information. No competing evidence names different parents.

---

### Source Classification

**Source 1 — Mauro Cruz Corona's 1910 civil birth registration (src_001)**

"México, Guerrero, Registro Civil, 1860-1996," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:Q5JL-M8X6), entrada para Mauro Cruz Corona y Sóstenes Cruz, 6 de diciembre de 1910; imagen digital, FamilySearch, citando registro original en el Archivo del Registro Civil de Guerrero, México.

Original source — a contemporaneous civil registration act created 6 December 1910, fourteen days after the birth event. The information regarding the child's name, birth date, birth place, and parentage is **primary**: reported to the registrar by Sóstenes Cruz, the father and declarant, who had firsthand knowledge of the event. The evidence bearing on both parent identities is **direct**: the record explicitly names Sóstenes Cruz as father and Apolinar Corona as mother. Note: the mother's surname is indexed as "Co??na" — two characters unclear in the original image — and is resolved by Source 2 below. Source class: **original / primary / direct**.

**Source 2 — Margarito Cruz Corona's 1908 civil birth registration (src_002)**

"México, Guerrero, Registro Civil, 1860-1996", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGW7-YQNS : accessed 16 September 2026), Entry for Cruz Corona and Sostenes Cruz, 17 de junio de 1908.

Original source — a civil registration act for Mauro's sibling Margarito Cruz Corona, born 10 June 1908 and registered 17 June 1908 at Montes de Oca, Guerrero. Informant was a household member, likely the father Sóstenes Cruz. The parentage information is **primary** and **direct**; this record spells "Apolinar Corona" clearly, resolving the uncertain character readings in Source 1. Source class: **original / primary / direct**.

**Source 3 — Mauro Cruz's 1941 Parácuaro Catholic marriage (src_003)**

"México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSF1-89NS : accessed 16 September 2026), Entry for Mauro Cruz and Sostenes Cruz, 20 de febrero de 1941.

Derivative source — FamilySearch index/transcription only; the underlying parish register image (ark:/61903/3:1:939L-9NX2-R) was not examined. Records Mauro Cruz, groom, marrying Esperanza Ramirez in Parácuaro, Michoacán, 21 February 1941. The groom himself provided his parents' names (Sostenes Cruz, father; Ma Apolinar Corona, mother) — **primary, direct** information about parentage from the subject himself, recorded in a contemporaneous ecclesiastical act. The source's derivative classification reflects the index-only access, not the quality of the underlying register's information. Source class: **derivative / primary / direct** (for the parentage claims).

**Source 4 — Liborio Cruz's 1940 Parácuaro Catholic marriage (src_004)**

"México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSF1-3G33 : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Liborio Cruz and Amparo Ortega, marriage 9 July 1940, Parácuaro, Michoacán, México.

Derivative source — index only; underlying image (ark:/61903/3:1:939L-9NXL-7) not examined. Records Liborio Cruz, Mauro's brother, marrying Amparo Ortega in Parácuaro, Michoacán, 9 July 1940. Liborio stated his father as "Sostanas" (given name only; surname Cruz inferred from family pattern, not stated in this index) and his mother as "Ma Apolinar Corona." The information is **secondary** (the groom reported a parent's name) and **direct** (the relationship is explicitly stated). Caution: the father's surname is not recorded in this index entry and is not asserted from this source alone. Source class: **derivative / secondary / direct**.

**Source 5 — Primitivo Cruz C's 1945 Arteaga Catholic marriage (src_005)**

"México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSJH-V5VG : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Primitivo Cruz C and Sostenes Cruz, 3 de marzo de 1945.

Derivative source — index only; underlying image (ark:/61903/3:1:939L-9Y9X-T4) not examined. Records Primitivo Cruz C, marrying Hilaria Ibarra in Arteaga, Michoacán, 3 March 1945. Primitivo stated his father as Sostenes Cruz and his mother as Apolinar Corona. The information is **secondary** (the groom reported parents' names) and **direct**. Groom's surname is indexed as "Cruz C" — the "C" likely abbreviates "Corona" (the maternal double-surname Cruz Corona); image review needed to confirm the full surname. Source class: **derivative / secondary / direct**.

---

### Evidence and Correlation

**The two original civil registrations establish the parentage from a single primary witness.** Mauro's 1910 birth record (src_001) names the father as Sóstenes Cruz and the mother as Apolinar Corona (a_005, a_006, a_007, a_010). Margarito's 1908 birth record (src_002) names the same parents (a_017, a_018, a_019, a_022). Both registrations were made in the Guerrero civil register by the official civil registrar within days of each birth. However, both records were almost certainly reported by the same declarant — Sóstenes Cruz, the father — meaning these two registrations represent one witness's account entered into the official register on two separate occasions, not two independent witnesses. Their principal evidential value is therefore the corroboration of the registrar's independent act of recording, and the clear spelling of "Apolinar Corona" in the 1908 sibling record, which resolves the uncertain "Co??na" reading in the 1910 record. Taken together they constitute strong evidence, while understood as one informant's account.

**The mother's surname.** Mauro's 1910 registration (src_001) indexes the mother's surname as "Co??na," indicating two characters unclear in the original image (a_010). The 1908 sibling registration (src_002) spells "Apolinar Corona" clearly and unambiguously (a_022). The 1908 record's spelling independently confirms the 1910 indexer's best reading as correct — "Corona."

**The three Catholic marriage records corroborate and extend the parentage across the identity gap.** Mauro Cruz himself, marrying in Parácuaro, Michoacán, in 1941, named Sostenes Cruz and Ma Apolinar Corona as his parents (a_029, a_030, a_037, a_039). This is the strongest possible corroboration for the parentage conclusion: the subject himself, in a contemporaneous ecclesiastical act in Michoacán, names the identical parents found in his 1910 Guerrero civil birth registration. His brother Liborio Cruz, marrying in Parácuaro in 1940, named the same mother (Ma Apolinar Corona) and a father whose given name "Sostanas" is a documented variant of "Sóstenes" (a_049, a_050). His sibling Primitivo Cruz C, marrying in Arteaga, Michoacán, in 1945, named Sostenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona as his parents (a_069, a_070, a_076, a_079). Across five records — two original civil registrations and three Catholic marriage index entries — the parental names are consistent: father Sóstenes/Sostenes/Sostanas Cruz, mother Apolinar/Ma Apolinar Corona.

---

### The Identity Question: Connecting the Guerrero Record to the Michoacán Subject

The research question was framed around a Mauro Cruz Corona associated with Nueva Italia, Michoacán, born about 1910. The two original civil registrations place both Mauro and his sibling Margarito in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero — geographically distinct from Nueva Italia, Michoacán. Hypothesis h_001 documents this discrepancy and assesses identity at "probable." Following the Michoacán Catholic church record search (CID 1883388), h_001 was updated to include the corroborating assertions from the three marriage records (a_029, a_030, a_037, a_039, a_049, a_050, a_069, a_070), and its notes were revised to reflect the post-search identity conclusion: the family's Guerrero→Michoacán migration trajectory is now documented through three independent marriage records of siblings across 1940–1945, with identity assessed at probable pending image review of the underlying parish registers.

The three Catholic marriage records from CID 1883388 substantially advance the identity resolution:

1. **Mauro Cruz's own 1941 marriage (src_003)** shows an adult male named Mauro Cruz marrying in Parácuaro, Michoacán, naming Sostenes Cruz and Ma Apolinar Corona as his parents — the same parents named on the 1910 Guerrero birth registration. The combination of an exact given name (Mauro), the same parents (both names, both variants consistent), and a Michoacán location consistent with the research subject's known associations provides strong corroboration of identity. The birth year discrepancy — approximately 1912 per the marriage record index versus 22 November 1910 per the civil registration — is explained by the index's derivation of birth year from age at marriage, a method rated indeterminate quality; the original civil registration, created fourteen days after the birth event by the father who was present, is the superior authority.

2. **Siblings Liborio (src_004) and Primitivo (src_005)** independently marry in the same Michoacán region, naming the same parents. Their presence in Parácuaro and Arteaga, Michoacán, from 1940 to 1945, establishes that the Cruz family — born in Guerrero's Tierra Caliente — relocated to Michoacán's Tierra Caliente, consistent with a well-documented regional migration pattern across the Guerrero–Michoacán border.

The identity conclusion is assessed at **probable**. The birthplace discrepancy between the original question's premise (Nueva Italia, Michoacán) and the civil registrations (La Unión, Guerrero) is explicable as a distinction between the family's birth locality (Guerrero, 1908–1910) and its later Michoacán residence (from some point before 1940). The original question's premise derived from secondary or oral information; the civil registrations are original primary documents. No competing Mauro Cruz Corona born about 1910 was found in any searched record set (Michoacán civil registration, 1930 Mexico census). The name combination "Mauro Cruz Corona" born in 1910 to a Cruz father and Corona mother is sufficiently distinctive within the searched record set to support the identification. The adult Mauro Cruz naming the same parents in 1941 Michoacán is the decisive identity bridge. Identity at proved is not claimed because the three Catholic marriage records are derivative sources (index only) and the 1941 record omits the maternal surname from the groom's name ("Cruz" rather than "Cruz Corona"), leaving a residual gap that image review of the original registers would close.

---

### Search Scope and Exhaustiveness

The subject's own original civil birth registration was found in Guerrero civil registration (CID 1918291). A sibling's registration corroborated the parentage from the same collection. The GPS mentor evaluation (ev_001) identified Michoacán Catholic church records (CID 1883388) as requiring search to address the identity gap; that search was completed and returned three marriage records (Mauro 1941, Liborio 1940, Primitivo 1945). Michoacán civil registration (CID 1916243) was searched with three name variants — no result. The 1930 Mexico National Census (CID 1307314) was searched — no result. Remaining unsearched items: the Ancestry alternate Michoacán civil registration index (collection 60415) and US border crossings (CID 1803932). Both are fallback or ancillary records — the Ancestry index is an alternate index of the same underlying records as CID 1916243 (already searched), and US border crossings are ancillary and cannot name different parents. No remaining unsearched record type in the confirmed event jurisdiction (Guerrero civil registration) or in the Michoacán Catholic church record set could plausibly overturn the stated parentage. Exhaustiveness declared.

---

### Conclusion Statement

The evidence strongly suggests that Mauro Cruz Corona, born 22 November 1910 in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico, was the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (father) and **Apolinar Corona** (mother). This conclusion is supported by five records — two original Guerrero civil birth registrations and three Michoacán Catholic marriage index entries — all naming the same parents consistently across a 37-year span and across two states. The subject himself named his parents in his 1941 Michoacán marriage record, providing the decisive corroboration that bridges the Guerrero birth and the Michoacán adult. The tier is **probable**: the parentage is well-supported at the primary source level, but the three Catholic marriage records are derivative (image review outstanding), and the identity correlation between the Guerrero-born child and the Michoacán-resident adult is established by derivative evidence for its final step. Image review of the three parish register images (ark:/61903/3:1:939L-9NX2-R, ark:/61903/3:1:939L-9NXL-7, ark:/61903/3:1:939L-9Y9X-T4) would consolidate the remaining derivative-source limitation and move this conclusion toward proved.

# Locality Research Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, Mexico (1900–1930)

## Jurisdiction

Nueva Italia de Ruiz is a city in the present-day municipio of Múgica, in the Tierra Caliente (Infiernillo subregion) of the state of Michoacán, Mexico. **However, Municipio de Múgica was not created until February 12, 1942.** During the target period 1900–1930, Nueva Italia was part of a predecessor jurisdiction — most likely **Apatzingán** — and civil registration records will be filed under that municipality in the statewide archive. Michoacán became a state on December 22, 1823.

Nueva Italia was established approximately 1900–1903 by the Cusi family as a large agricultural colony in the Tepalcatepec river basin. Its founding population drew settlers from various parts of Michoacán and Jalisco.

## Primary Records, 1900–1930

### 1. Michoacán Civil Registration — TOP PRIORITY
- **[Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1916243)** (FamilySearch, CID 1916243) — **indexed & images**. Covers births, marriages, and deaths organized by state then municipality. Coverage estimated at 90–95% of population. Browse under **Apatzingán** (not Múgica, which did not exist until 1942). Birth records name child, both parents, grandparents, parental ages and civil status. ([How to use](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoacan,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records))
- **Ancestry parallel indexes** (same underlying records, different index):
  - [Births 1859–1934](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60415/) (Ancestry, collection 60415) — index & images ($)
  - [Deaths 1859–1935](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60465/) (Ancestry, collection 60465) — index & images ($)
  - [Marriages 1859–1940](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60437/) (Ancestry, collection 60437) — index & images ($)

### 2. Catholic Church Records — PARALLEL SOURCE
- **[Mexico, Michoacan and Michoacan, Catholic Church Records, 1555-1996](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1883388)** (FamilySearch, CID 1883388) — **index only**, coverage varies. Baptismal registers naming both parents and godparents.
- **[Mexico Baptisms, 1560-1950](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1473011)** (FamilySearch, CID 1473011) — index only; partial/sampled coverage of Michoacán.
- **[Michoacán, Mexico, Catholic Church Records, 1649-1909](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60021)** (Ancestry, collection 60021) — images ($).
- Church records for Tierra Caliente fall under the Archdiocese of Morelia (Arquidiócesis de Morelia). Search neighboring parish records (Apatzingán, Gabriel Zamora) if the Nueva Italia parish record is missing.

### 3. 1930 Mexico National Census — HIGH VALUE
- **[Mexico National Census, 1930](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1307314)** (FamilySearch, CID 1307314) — **indexed & images**. A person born ~1910 would appear here at approximately age 20. Provides household context, parents' names, birthplace, and marital status. Also at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1771) ($).

### 4. Border Crossing Records — SUPPLEMENTARY
- **[US Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1903-1957](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1803932)** (FamilySearch, CID 1803932) — index. Tierra Caliente families frequently crossed north for agricultural work; these records often list birthplace, age, and parents or relatives in Mexico.
- **[Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1895-1964](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082)** (Ancestry) — index & images ($).

## Online Coverage Assessment

|---|---|---|
| Michoacán Civil Registration 1859–1940 | **Indexed + images** | Browse under Apatzingán, not Múgica |
| Michoacán Catholic Church Records | **Index only** | Coverage varies by parish |

## Physical / Offline Repositories

- **Michoacán Civil Registry State Archives** — physical originals; contact through [Archivo General del Estado de Michoacán](https://archivos.gob.mx/DirectorioArchivos/DirectorioArchivos.html).
- **63 historical archives** in 55 Michoacán municipalities: [List of Michoacán Historical Archives](https://sic.gob.mx/lista.php?table=archivo&disciplina=&estado_id=16).
- **Archivo General de la Nación de México**: http://www.agn.gob.mx/

## Neighboring Jurisdictions to Search

Nueva Italia lies near the border of Apatzingán and Gabriel Zamora (Lombardía) municipios, and is within 100–150 km of the Colima and Jalisco state borders. When a record is not found in the expected municipio:
- Search **Apatzingán** and **Gabriel Zamora** civil registration under CID 1916243.
- Search **Jalisco** civil registration (CID 1918187, 1857–2000) for families of settler origin.
- Search **Colima** records (CID 1916241) for events near the state border.

## Language and Script

All records are in Spanish. Early civil entries are handwritten in narrative style; later registers use formatted columnar forms. Resources:
- [Spanish Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List)
- [BYU Spanish Script Tutorial](https://script.byu.edu/spanish-handwriting/introduction)
